what_its_for: Ribociclib is used to treat a certain type of breast cancer called hormone receptor-positive (HR+), HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer. It is usually taken together with another hormone-blocking medicine. It works by slowing or stopping the growth of cancer cells.
how_to_take: Take ribociclib by mouth once a day for 21 days in a row, followed by 7 days off. This 28-day cycle repeats as long as your doctor tells you to continue. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablets whole — do not chew, crush, or split them. Try to take it at the same time each day, preferably in the morning.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 3 tablets (600 mg total) taken once a day for 21 days, then 7 days off. Your doctor may lower your dose if you experience side effects. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at your regular time the next day. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take an extra dose — just continue with your next scheduled dose.
storage: Store ribociclib at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original container and protect it from moisture and light. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid any medicines that can cause serious heart rhythm problems (ask your doctor or pharmacist for a full list). Tell your doctor about all prescription, over-the-counter, herbal, and vitamin supplements you take, since many medicines can interact with ribociclib. Avoid becoming pregnant — use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a fast, slow, or irregular heartbeat or feel faint or dizzy; signs of a serious infection such as fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, chills, or body aches; unusual bruising or bleeding; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, or stomach pain; severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that will not stop; or shortness of breath. Also call your doctor if you have any new or worsening symptoms that worry you.
when_it_works: Ribociclib does not cure cancer, but it can slow the growth of cancer cells and help you live longer with the disease. You may not feel any different at first, but your doctor will check if the medicine is working through regular blood tests and scans. It is important to keep taking it as prescribed, even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not take ribociclib if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can harm an unborn baby. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 3 weeks after your last dose. Liver problems: Your dose may need to be lowered if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Your doctor will monitor your liver with regular blood tests. Older adults: Older adults can take ribociclib, but they may be more sensitive to side effects, so close monitoring is important. Always tell your doctor about all your health conditions before starting this medicine.
